software_initialization_sequence: 1. After hardware reset, CCCR.INIT = 1 (reset value); m_can_tx = recessive.
2. Set CCCR.CCE = 1 to enable write access to protected configuration registers (requires CCCR.INIT = 1).
3. (Recommended if Message RAM has ECC/parity) Initialize Message RAM by writing 0x00000000 to each word to create valid ECC checksums.
4. Program NBTP (Nominal Bit Timing): NBRP / NTSEG1 / NTSEG2 / NSJW.
5. Program DBTP (Data Bit Timing): DBRP / DTSEG1 / DTSEG2 / DSJW (only used in CAN FD with BRS = 1). Also set DBTP.TDC = 1 if Transmitter Delay Compensation needed.
6. Program TDCR (TDCO + TDCF) if TDC enabled.
7. Program GFC, SIDFC, XIDFC, XIDAM (Acceptance Filter Configuration).
8. Program RXF0C / RXF1C / RXBC / RXESC (Rx FIFO 0 / 1 + Rx Buffer + Rx Element Size).
9. Program TXBC / TXESC / TXEFC (Tx Buffers + Tx Element Size + Tx Event FIFO).
10. Program CCCR: NISO, TXP, EFBI, PXHD, WMM, UTSU, BRSE, FDOE, DAR. Leave INIT + CCE = 1 during this step.
11. (Optional) Program TSCC, TOCC, IE, ILS, ILE, TXBTIE, TXBCIE.
12. Initialize Message RAM filter list elements + Rx Buffer + Tx Buffer / Tx Event FIFO start positions consistently with SIDFC / XIDFC / RXBC / TXBC / TXEFC.
14. Clear CCCR.INIT to enter normal operation. CPU must wait for INIT to read back 0 (clock-domain-crossing delay) before further operations.
15. BSP waits for 11 consecutive recessive bits (Bus_Idle) before joining bus.
typical_classical_data_frame_transmit_se: 1. Host writes Tx Buffer element (T0: ESI/XTD/RTR/ID; T1: MM/EFC/TSCE/FDF=0/BRS=ignored/DLC; T2..Tn: data bytes).
2. Host writes TXBAR.AR_n = 1 to add transmission request for Buffer n.
3. M_CAN Tx Handler scans Tx Buffers, picks lowest-Message-ID; updates TXBRP.TRP_n = 1.
4. At next Bus_Idle (≥ 11 consecutive recessive bits): drive SOF (1 dominant) — all nodes hard-synchronize.

5. Drive 11-bit IDENTIFIER (or 29-bit if XTD = 1: 11-ID + SRR + IDE + 18-ID) + RTR bit (ARBITRATION FIELD); on each bit monitor bus. Recessive driven + dominant monitored → LOSE arbitration, withdraw, become receiver.
7. Drive DATA FIELD (0..8 bytes from T2..T3, MSB first per byte).
8. Drive 15-bit CRC SEQUENCE + recessive CRC DELIMITER.
9. Drive recessive ACK SLOT; sample bus; expect dominant ACK from at least one receiver. Otherwise raise ACKNOWLEDGMENT ERROR.
10. Drive recessive ACK DELIMITER + 7 recessive END OF FRAME bits.
12. (if error-passive) Drive 8 recessive SUSPEND TRANSMISSION bits before next transmission.
13. (if CCCR.TXP = 1) Wait additional 2 bit times after own successful transmission.
14. Set TXBRP.TRP_n = 0 + TXBTO.TO_n = 1; raise IR.TC if TXBTIE.TIE_n = 1.
15. (if T1.EFC = 1) Write Tx Event FIFO element with Message ID + TX timestamp + Message Marker + ET = 01.
typical_can_fd_data_frame_transmit_seque: 1..3. Same as Classical sequence — but Tx Buffer T1 has FDF = 1 + BRS = 1; ESI computed by OR of T0.ESI and error-passive flag.
4. Wait Bus_Idle → drive SOF (1 dominant) → hard-sync.
5. Drive IDENTIFIER + RRS (always dominant) + IDE (if 29-bit: + SRR + 18-bit-ID + RRS).
6a. Drive r1 (dominant) + FDF = 1 (recessive) + res (dominant) + BRS = 1 (recessive). All at NBTP rate.
6b. At BRS bit's sample point: switch to DBTP bit time. ESI + DLC[3:0] transmitted at DBTP rate.
7. Drive DATA FIELD (0..64 bytes per DLC encoding) at DBTP rate.
8b. Drive 17-bit (≤16 B) or 21-bit (>16 B) CRC SEQUENCE at DBTP rate.
9. At CRC DELIMITER bit: switch back to NBTP rate; drive recessive CRC DELIMITER.
10. Drive ACK SLOT (recessive); CAN FD ACK timing accounts for transmitter delay — at SSP-aware bit time. Sample bus for dominant.
11. Drive ACK DELIMITER (recessive) + 7-bit EOF (all recessive) + 3-bit INTERMISSION.
12. PSR.TDCV updated with measured SSP position.
13. (if T1.EFC = 1) Write Tx Event FIFO element with FDF + BRS = 1 + ET = 01.

Same as classical sequence except T1 has FDF = 1, BRS = 0. Whole frame transmitted at NBTP rate; CAN FD CRC (17 or 21 bit) instead of 15-bit; DLC encoding per CAN FD table; RRS replaces RTR (no remote frames in FD).
typical_remote_frame_sequence_classical_: 1. Host writes Tx Buffer T0.RTR = 1, T1.FDF = 0 (classical only), T1.DLC = 0 (no DATA).
2. M_CAN transmits Classical remote frame per ISO 11898-1:2015 even if CCCR.FDOE = 1.
3. Node holding the matching DATA FRAME responds with DATA FRAME (same IDENTIFIER).
4. If a DATA FRAME and matching REMOTE FRAME start simultaneously, DATA FRAME wins (RTR dominant beats RTR recessive).
typical_receive_sequence: 1. Receiver detects SOF dominant bit (passes CCCR.EFBI filter if = 1); hard-synchronizes.
2. Sample IDENTIFIER + RTR (or RRS in FD) + IDE + extended bits.
3. At FDF bit position: dominant → Classical CAN path; recessive → CAN FD path.
4. (FD only) Detect res bit: if res = 1 → Protocol Exception (PSR.PXE + PSR.ACT = 00) when CCCR.PXHD = 0; FORM ERROR if PXHD = 1.
5. (FD only) Detect BRS bit: if BRS = 1 → switch to DBTP bit time + SSP-based bit error checking; else stay at NBTP.
6. Receive DATA FIELD per DLC; receive CRC15 / CRC17 / CRC21 + (ISO FD) stuff-count parity; compare.
7. (FD with BRS = 1) At CRC delimiter sample point: switch back to NBTP bit time.
8. If CRC matched and message reaches last-but-one bit of EOF: drive dominant ACK on ACK SLOT and validate message.
9. Apply Acceptance Filter: sequentially match against SIDFC / XIDFC filter elements; first match decides storage destination (FIFO0 / FIFO1 / Rx Buffer / debug / reject / set-priority).
10. Write Rx FIFO / Rx Buffer element; update Put Index / Fill Level / New Data flag.
11. Raise IR.RFnN / IR.DRX / IR.HPM as appropriate.
12. (Sync message with CCCR.UTSU = 1 + filter SSYNC/ESYNC = 1) Pulse m_can_tsrx.
13. (Filter event pins enabled via SFID2[8:6] / EFID2[8:6]) Pulse m_can_fe[2:0] bits.
14. If CRC mismatch: at the bit following ACK DELIMITER, start transmitting an ERROR FLAG.
arbitration_loss_sequence: 1. Two transmitters start simultaneously on Bus_Idle.
2. On each ARBITRATION FIELD bit, each compares its driven bit to bus.
3. The first time a transmitter drives recessive but reads dominant: it loses arbitration.
4. Loser withdraws (stops driving) and becomes a receiver of the winner's frame.
5. Loser may retry retransmission once the bus is idle again (unless CCCR.DAR = 1).
6. In DAR mode: TXBRP.TRP_n cleared on arbitration loss + TXBCF.CF_n set.
error_signalling_sequence: 1. Error-active node detects BIT/STUFF/FORM/ACK error during a frame.
2. At the next bit, transmit ACTIVE ERROR FLAG (6 dominant bits).
3. Other nodes detect this and transmit their own ACTIVE ERROR FLAG; superposition results in 6..12 dominant bits.
4. After ERROR FLAG, transmit ERROR DELIMITER (8 recessive bits).
5. PSR.LEC (arbitration phase) or PSR.DLEC (FD data phase) updated; IR.PEA / IR.PED raised.
6. Original transmitter automatically retransmits the message once bus is idle (unless CCCR.DAR = 1).
7. CRC errors specifically: ERROR FLAG starts at the bit following ACK DELIMITER (not immediately).
fault_confinement_transition_sequence: 1. error-active → error-passive: when TX_ERR_COUNT ≥ 128 OR RX_ERR_COUNT ≥ 128. PSR.EP = 1; IR.EP raised; CAN FD ESI in transmitted frames forced recessive.
2. error-passive → bus-off: when TX_ERR_COUNT = 256. PSR.BO = 1; IR.BO raised; CCCR.INIT set automatically.
3. error-passive → error-active: when both TX_ERR_COUNT and RX_ERR_COUNT ≤ 127.

4. bus-off → error-active: after CPU clears CCCR.INIT, M_CAN waits for 129 occurrences of Bus_Idle (129 × 11 consecutive recessive bits); both error counts reset to 0; PSR.LEC updated to Bit0Error per 11-recessive sequence to track progress.
tx_event_handling_sequence: 1. Tx Handler completes transmission (or transmission-in-spite-of-cancellation in DAR mode).
2. If Tx Buffer T1.EFC = 1, write Tx Event FIFO element at TXEFS.EFPI.
4. If watermark TXEFC.EFWM reached: IR.TEFW raised.
5. If TXEFS.EFFL = TXEFC.EFS: TXEFS.EFF = 1 (full); IR.TEFF raised.
6. Host reads Tx Event FIFO element at TXEFS.EFGI; writes EFGI value (or last-read index) to TXEFA.EFAI → M_CAN sets EFGI = EFAI + 1, EFFL decremented.
transmit_cancellation_sequence: 1. Host writes TXBCR.CR_n = 1 (dedicated or Tx Queue Buffer only — NOT Tx FIFO).
2. If Buffer n transmission has not yet started: TXBRP.TRP_n cleared; TXBCF.CF_n set; TXBTO.TO_n not set.
3. If transmission ongoing: bit remains pending until done; on success → TXBTO.TO_n + TXBCF.CF_n both set; on disturbance → only TXBCF.CF_n set.
5. (DAR mode + success-in-spite-of-cancellation): Tx Event FIFO element written with ET = 10 (= transmission in spite of cancellation).
power_down_sequence: 1. CPU asserts m_can_clkstop_req or sets CCCR.CSR = 1.
2. M_CAN completes any pending transmission, waits for Bus_Idle.
5. External clock controller may stop m_can_hclk + m_can_cclk.
6. To wake: restart clocks → CPU deasserts m_can_clkstop_req or clears CCCR.CSR.
8. CPU clears CCCR.INIT → BSP synchronizes to bus (11 consecutive recessive bits).
tdc_per_frame_sequence_with_BRS: 1. CCCR.FDOE = 1 + CCCR.BRSE = 1 + Tx Buffer FDF = 1 + BRS = 1 + DBTP.TDC = 1.
2. Transmit FD frame: at FDF → res falling edge on m_can_tx, start delay counter (clocked by m_can_cclk).
3. Stop counter when same edge seen on m_can_rx.
4. SSP_position = measured_delay + TDCR.TDCO (rounded down to mtq).
5. If TDCR.TDCF > 0: ignore m_can_rx dominant edges before SSP_position ≥ TDCF.
6. Use SSP for bit-error check in data phase (BRS → CRC delimiter sample point).
7. PSR.TDCV updated to current SSP position (visible to host).
acceptance_filter_sequence_for_high_prio: 1. Configure filter element with SFEC / EFEC = 100 (set-priority no storage) OR 101 (set-priority + store FIFO0) OR 110 (set-priority + store FIFO1).
2. Receiver matches incoming frame against filter element.
3. Match: update HPMS register with FLST (0 std / 1 ext), FIDX (filter index), MSI (00 no FIFO / 01 lost / 10 FIFO0 / 11 FIFO1), BIDX (Rx FIFO buffer index).
5. Host CPU reads HPMS, fast-paths the high-priority message.
debug_on_can_dma_sequence: 1. Configure 3 filter elements with SFEC / EFEC = 111 + SFID2 / EFID2[10:9] = 01 (A), 10 (B), 11 (C).
2. Configure 3 consecutive Rx Buffers (e.g. RxBuffer #61, #62, #63) to store debug messages A/B/C.
6. Receive debug C → DMS = 11 → m_can_dma_req asserted.
7. DMA controller reads the 3 Rx Buffers from Message RAM.
8. DMA controller asserts m_can_dma_ack → m_can_dma_req deasserted → DMS = 00.
